title: Useful-Life Table for Security Deposit Account Replacement Charges
content:
When a carpet, paint, flooring, blinds or appliance item is replaced at move-out, its charge on the Security Deposit Account is depreciated. This table gives the useful life of each item class, in months, and the depreciation method, for every deposit program.

| Item class | Zero-Deposit Guarantee Plan | Reduced Deposit Plan | Standard Deposit Plan | Premier Residence Deposit Plan | Conditional Approval Deposit Plan | Enhanced Deposit Plan |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Carpet (months) | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |
| Interior paint (months) | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| Vinyl plank and hard flooring (months) | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 |
| Window blinds (months) | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |
| Kitchen and laundry appliances (months) | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 120 |
| Depreciation method | straight line, monthly | straight line, monthly | straight line, monthly | straight line, monthly | straight line, monthly | straight line, monthly |

**Straight line, monthly.** An item loses an equal share of its value for each month of its useful life. After 60 months, a carpet or blinds item has used its whole life. Paint does so after 36 months, and flooring or an appliance after 120 months.

**Worked comparison (hypothetical ages).** Take one hypothetical age of 30 months:

| Item | Useful life | Months remaining | Share of life remaining |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carpet | 60 | 30 | one half |
| Paint | 36 | 6 | one sixth |
| Flooring | 120 | 90 | three quarters |
